Yes. One paper directly studies LLM synthetic slate preference for recommendation: it asks whether LLMs can express pairwise preferences between slates for synthetic A/B testing, and finds that LLM-based synthetic preferences can recover stable rankings when combined with a generalized Rao-Kupper model [4]. It frames this as a screening stage before live experiments, not a replacement for real A/B testing [4].

Related slate recommendation papers focus on generating and aligning slates with user preferences rather than using LLMs as synthetic preference judges. OGR uses list-wise preference planning and reward-guided optimization to align generated slates with user preferences [1], while HiGR uses hierarchical planning and listwise alignment for ranking fidelity, user interest, and diversity at industrial scale [2]. A broader recommendation paper also shows principled synthetic data can help LLMs learn generalizable user preference patterns, but it is not specifically about slate preference evaluation [6].
